text:
Marta: Quick RFC follow-up — I'm proposing we extract the call-path router from runtime-hotpath into a tiny independent service (call-path-svc) to reduce coupling and make incremental rollouts easier. Thoughts?

Jamie: curious about perf hit. do you have numbers on added RPC latency vs current in-process routing? :thinking_face:

Marta: good q — rough numbers from the spike: current median routing cost ~0.4ms, RPC hop adds ~0.9ms on our intra-AZ infra. so ~1.3ms median. worst-case tail increases more but still within 99th SLO we set for routing (5ms). full numbers in the spike doc: https://go/eng/call-path-spike (attached).

Srini: tradeoffs look familiar — we get clearer ownership + easier feature flags, but we risk increasing token cost if we can't batch before routing. how do you plan to keep batching/caching behavior intact?

Marta: plan is to keep prefix KV caching in the runtime; call-path-svc only answers route decisions (model variant + placement + policy). runtime still performs batching. call-path-svc will be extremely lightweight: simple memcache + policy engine.

Alex: how will we handle fallbacks if call-path-svc is down? we need graceful degradation to a safe default route, not fail the request.

Marta: agreed. proposed fallback hierarchy in RFC: 1) local cached decision (stale ok), 2) default route config (from config store), 3) last-known-good mapping per tenant. We'll also add a short-circuit mode so runtime can route using the old in-process logic during incidents.

Nora: rollout plan? this seems risky to flip cluster-wide.

Marta: phased: dev / canary -> tenant opt-in -> gradual ramp by traffic percent -> auto-rollback on quality or latency regression. We'll gate by two checks in the console: latency delta and error budget burn. Also plan an A/B where 10% uses call-path-svc, 90% in-process for 48h before expanding.

Jamie: makes sense. need a smoke test matrix: latency, CPU on runtime, error rate, QPS, batching efficiency. can we add an e2e perf test in CI that runs a synthetic workload?

Srini: also add evals: compare model selection distribution pre/post for a prompt corpus. if we suddenly pick smaller models more often we could regress quality. tie to evals infra.

Marta: yep — will add a regression alert that looks at model variant distribution + eval set output diffs. If quality drops by >1.5% on the signal set -> rollback.

Alex: what about retries? extra network hop increases chance of transient failures. should we implement an idempotent, idempotency-keyed request pattern or just rely on rpc client retries?

Marta: rpc client will do bounded retries with exponential backoff (max 2 retries). we will make the call-path RPC idempotent (pure function of request context + cache). also instrument retries in tracing so we can correlate with user-facing latency.

Nora: security/compliance note: if call-path-svc contains tenant routing policies, ensure its logs don't leak PII and route decisions are audited. KMS keys for configs?

Marta: config and audit logs will be in control plane with RBAC — also only store tenant ids and policy ids, not prompt content. integrate with our existing KMS/HSM for config secrets.

Jamie: can we do an initial internal-only release (no external traffic) to exercise scaling? i.e., run call-path-svc behind a toggle for staging and run shadow traffic from prod for 24h.

Marta: yes — shadowing for 24h + load tests to 2x peak. we'll also run a stress test with synthetic KV churn to validate memcache eviction behavior.

Srini: any changes to the model catalog API? call-path-svc will need to consult model profiles. do we version that API first?

Marta: we'll bump the model-catalog contract to v2 read-only for now — call-path-svc reads model profiles via stable endpoint. write path unchanged. versioning details in the RFC doc.

Alex: owner and timeline?

Marta: owner: @Marta (me) + @Jamie for runtime changes + @Srini for policy engine. timeline: prototype in 2w, canary in 6w, tenant opt-ins start at week 10.

deploy-bot: Deployed canary image call-path-svc:v0.1 to staging at 1845678925 :rocket:

Jamie: I'll add the smoke tests and perf CI job. opening PRs: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/7890 and https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/7891

Srini: I'll wire eval alerts (ENG-4321) and add model distribution dashboards.

Nora: I'll review audit/logging plan and kick off compliance checklist.

Marta: thanks all. I'll update the RFC with the rollout table and a rollback checklist. tagging folks for follow-ups: @Jamie @Srini @Nora. :thumbsup:
